note: A 27-year-old studying nursing prerequisites while working part-time is not a business owner, physician or equivalent, and income fails on the hardest available evidence: a $5,000 personal credit limit against a $6,000 price, a single household account held by his wife, and her refusal on the grounds that it exceeds their monthly house payment. On starting point he is the opposite of good-to-great — he has never been in shape and says so directly: 'I don't even know what my body would look like' and 'I've never been happy with myself.' He does match on the other two: health is genuinely the neglected area, displaced by a new baby, a career change and study, and he is not the deconditioned gym-averse exclusion — he walks daily, owns kettlebells, and wants to build a home gym. This is the third consecutive prospect in this batch to sit outside the stated ICP on the same three criteria, and the second of those to close. Across the batch the pattern is now hard to dismiss: this rep's closes come from outside the written ICP and turn on emotional resonance and accountability need rather than on the success-and-income profile the company describes to prospects on live calls. Whether that is a targeting failure or an ICP-definition failure is a decision for the principal, but it should not be read as evidence of fit — this deal closed on an account whose holder had refused it.
